title: Wave 3 Person-by-Person Classical Mediterranean, Phoenicia/Carthage, Hellenistic Kingdoms, Alba Longa (14 Kings), 7 Kings of Rome & Julio-Claudian/Paschale Families

nodes.name: King Abibaal of Tyre (Father of Hiram I, Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.notes: Father of Solomon's ally King Hiram I.

nodes.name: King Hiram I of Tyre (980–947 BCE; Ally of David & Solomon, 1 Kgs 5)
nodes.era: 980–947 BCE (1 Kgs 5; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.role: King of Tyre & Lebanon Cedar Ally
nodes.notes: Son of Abibaal; supplied cedar and craftsman Huram-Abi for Solomon's Temple.

nodes.name: King Baal-ezer I of Tyre (Son of Hiram I, 946–930 BCE)
nodes.notes: Succeeded Hiram I through Abdastartus.

nodes.name: King Baal-ezer II of Tyre (Son of Ethbaal I; Brother of Jezebel, 846–841 BCE)
nodes.era: 846–841 BCE (Kurkh Monolith; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18)
nodes.role: Son of Ethbaal & Brother of Queen Jezebel
nodes.notes: Paid tribute to Shalmaneser III in 841 BCE.

nodes.name: King Mattan I of Tyre (Father of Pygmalion & Queen Dido, 840–832 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Baal-ezer II; father of Pygmalion and Elissa/Dido.

nodes.name: King Pygmalion / Pumayyaton of Tyre (Brother of Dido, 831–785 BCE)
nodes.era: 831–785 BCE (Josephus Ag. Ap. I.18; Nora Stone)
nodes.notes: Reigned 47 years; sister Elissa/Dido founded Carthage in his 7th year (814 BCE).

nodes.name: General Hamilcar Barca (First Punic War & Iberia, d. 228 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Hannibal, Hasdrubal, and Mago Barca.

nodes.name: Hannibal Barca of Carthage (247–183 BCE; Crossed Alps 218 BCE)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Hamilcar Barca; victor of Trebia, Trasimene & Cannae.

nodes.name: Hasdrubal Barca (Brother of Hannibal; Commander in Hispania, d. 207 BCE)
nodes.notes: Fell at the Battle of the Metaurus.

nodes.name: Mago Barca (Youngest Son of Hamilcar Barca, d. 203 BCE)
nodes.notes: Founded Port Mahon and fought in Italy.

nodes.name: General Hasdrubal Gisco (Father of Sophonisba, d. 202 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Sophonisba.

nodes.name: Queen Sophonisba (Daughter of Hasdrubal Gisco; Wife of Syphax & Masinissa)
nodes.notes: Married Numidian kings Syphax and Masinissa during the 2nd Punic War.

nodes.name: King Gaia of the Massylii (Father of Masinissa, d. 206 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of unifier King Masinissa.

nodes.name: King Masinissa of Numidia (202–148 BCE; Ally of Rome at Zama)
nodes.notes: Allied with Scipio Africanus at Zama; father of Micipsa, Mastanabal & Gulussa.

nodes.name: King Micipsa of Numidia (148–118 BCE; Adoptive Father of Jugurtha)
nodes.notes: Father of Adherbal & Hiempsal I; adopted nephew Jugurtha.

nodes.name: King Jugurtha of Numidia (Nephew of Micipsa, 118–104 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mastanabal; resisted Rome in the Jugurthine War.

nodes.name: King Juba I of Numidia (Father of Juba II, d. 46 BCE)
nodes.notes: Allied with Cato & Scipio at Thapsus; father of scholar-king Juba II.

nodes.name: King Ptolemy of Mauretania (Son of Juba II & Cleopatra Selene II, 23–40 CE)
nodes.era: c. 10 BCE – 40 CE (Tacitus Annals IV.23; Suetonius Caligula 35)
nodes.notes: Son of King Juba II and Queen Cleopatra Selene II; grandson of Mark Antony & Cleopatra VII!

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra Selene II (Daughter of Cleopatra VII & Mark Antony; Wife of Juba II)
nodes.notes: Twin daughter of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony; raised by Octavia Minor in Rome, wed King Juba II of Mauretania, and bore King Ptolemy of Mauretania.

nodes.name: King Gyges of Lydia (Mermnad Founder, 680–644 BCE)
nodes.notes: Overthrew Heraclid Candaules; allied with Assyria under Ashurbanipal.

nodes.name: King Ardys II of Lydia (644–624 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Gyges.

nodes.name: King Sadyattes of Lydia (624–612 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Alyattes.

nodes.name: King Alyattes of Lydia (612–560 BCE; Coinage Pioneer)
nodes.notes: Minted earliest electrum coins; wed daughter Aryenis to Median Crown Prince Astyages.

nodes.name: King Croesus of Lydia (560–546 BCE; Conquered by Cyrus)
nodes.notes: Famed for wealth; fought Cyrus the Great at Thymbra & Sardis (546 BCE).

nodes.name: Queen Aryenis of Media (Daughter of Alyattes; Wife of Astyages, Herodotus I.74)
nodes.notes: Married Astyages of Media to seal the Battle of the Eclipse peace treaty (585 BCE).

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus I Nicator (312–281 BCE; Husband of Apama)
nodes.notes: General of Alexander; wed Sogdian princess Apama.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus I Soter (281–261 BCE)
nodes.notes: Co-regent in Babylon & victor over Galatians.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus II Theos (261–246 BCE; Husband of Laodice & Berenice)
nodes.notes: Married Ptolemaic princess Berenice (Daniel 11:6 'King of the North').

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus II Callinicus (246–225 BCE)
nodes.role: Son of Antiochus II & Laodice I
nodes.notes: Father of Seleucus III & Antiochus III.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus III the Great (223–187 BCE; Dan 11:11)
nodes.notes: Restored Seleucid authority east to Bactria/India; wed daughter Cleopatra I Syra to Ptolemy V.

nodes.name: Emperor Seleucus IV Philopator (187–175 BCE; 2 Macc 3)
nodes.notes: Dispatched Heliodorus to Jerusalem Temple.

nodes.name: Emperor Demetrius I Soter (161–150 BCE; 1 Macc 7)
nodes.notes: Authorized High Priest Alcimus against Judas Maccabeus.

nodes.name: Queen Apama of Sogdia (Daughter of Spitamenes; Wife of Seleucus I)
nodes.role: Sogdian Queen of the Seleucid Empire
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sogdian leader Spitamenes; sole Alexander-era queen marriage never repudiated.

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra I Syra of Egypt (Daughter of Antiochus III; Wife of Ptolemy V)
nodes.role: Seleucid Princess Who Brought Name 'Cleopatra' to Egypt
nodes.notes: Introduced Seleucid marriage link and name Cleopatra into the Ptolemaic house.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus IV Epiphanes (175–164 BCE; Sparked Maccabean Revolt)
nodes.notes: Desecrated the Second Temple in 167 BCE, provoking Mattathias & Judas Maccabeus.

nodes.name: Emperor Antiochus V Eupator (Son of Antiochus IV, 164–161 BCE)
nodes.notes: Young son of Antiochus IV.

nodes.name: King Antigonus I Monophthalmus (d. 301 BCE at Ipsus)
nodes.notes: Unifier of Asia until Battle of Ipsus.

nodes.name: King Demetrius I Poliorcetes (337–283 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Antigonus II Gonatas.

nodes.name: King Antigonus II Gonatas of Macedon (277–239 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Demetrius Poliorcetes.

nodes.name: King Philip V of Macedon (221–179 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of final king Perseus.

nodes.name: King Perseus of Macedon (Last King of Macedon, 179–168 BCE; Pydna)
nodes.notes: Defeated by Aemilius Paullus at Pydna (168 BCE) and interned at Alba Fucens.

nodes.name: King Pyrrhus of Epirus (319–272 BCE; Aeacid Cousin of Alexander)
nodes.role: Molossian King Claiming Descent From Achilles
nodes.notes: Son of Aeacides; second cousin of Alexander the Great and renowned adversary of Rome ('Pyrrhic victory').

nodes.name: King Mithridates I Ktistes of Pontus (281–266 BCE)
nodes.notes: Claimed Achaemenid Persian noble lineage.

nodes.name: King Pharnaces I of Pontus (185–155 BCE)
nodes.notes: Captured Sinope.

nodes.name: King Mithridates VI Eupator ('The Great' / Poison King, 120–63 BCE)
nodes.notes: Fought three Mithridatic Wars against Sulla, Lucullus & Pompey; father of Cleopatra of Pontus & Pharnaces II.

nodes.name: King Pharnaces II of Pontus & Bosporus (Son of Mithridates VI; Battle of Zela 47 BCE)
nodes.notes: Son of Mithridates VI defeated by Julius Caesar at Zela (47 BCE).

nodes.name: Queen Cleopatra of Pontus (Daughter of Mithridates VI; Wife of Tigranes the Great)
nodes.era: fl. 94–66 BCE (Plutarch Lucullus; Betham Tab. LXXXIII)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Mithridates VI; married Tigranes II the Great of Armenia and bore Artavasdes II.

nodes.name: King Artaxias I of Armenia (189–160 BCE; Founder of Artaxata)
nodes.notes: Established Artaxiad Dynasty & capital Artaxata.

nodes.name: Emperor Tigranes II the Great of Armenia (95–55 BCE; King of Kings)
nodes.notes: Built empire from Caspian to Syria; wed Cleopatra of Pontus.

nodes.name: King Artavasdes II of Armenia (55–34 BCE; Son of Tigranes II)
nodes.notes: Scholarly son of Tigranes the Great & Cleopatra of Pontus.

nodes.name: King Diodotus I Soter of Bactria (250–239 BCE)
nodes.notes: Broke away from Antiochus II in Bactria/Sogdia.

nodes.name: King Euthydemus I of Bactria (230–200 BCE)
nodes.role: Defender of Bactra Against Antiochus III
nodes.notes: Father of Indo-Greek conqueror Demetrius I.

nodes.name: King Demetrius I of Bactria (c. 200–180 BCE; Conqueror of Gandhara)
nodes.notes: Extended Hellenistic rule into Northwest India.

nodes.name: King Menander I Soter / King Milinda (165–130 BCE; Milinda Panha)
nodes.notes: Central royal interlocutor of Buddhist classic Milinda Panha.

nodes.name: King Aegialeus of Sicyon (1st King in Eusebius Chronicle, p. 53)
nodes.era: Eusebius Chronicle p.53 (Synchronized With Belus & Ninus)
nodes.role: First Attested Greek City-King in Eusebius
nodes.notes: Son of Inachus in Apollodorus; placed by Eusebius at the dawn of Greek chronology as contemporary of Nimrod/Belus & Ninus.

nodes.name: King Abgar V Ukkama of Osroene / Edessa (4 BCE–7 CE, 13–50 CE)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Edessa — Eusebius HE I.13; Doctrine of Addai)
nodes.notes: Abgarid king of Edessa prominent in early Syriac Christian historiography.

nodes.name: King Latinus of Laurentum (Father of Lavinia, Dionysius I.57–64)
nodes.era: 12th c. BCE (Dionysius Ant. I.57–64; Livy I.1)
nodes.notes: Welcomed Aeneas and gave daughter Lavinia in marriage.

nodes.name: Queen Lavinia (Daughter of Latinus; Wife of Aeneas; Mother of Silvius)
nodes.role: Latin Princess & Mother of Alban Dynasty
nodes.notes: Eponym of Lavinium; mother of Silvius Posthumus by Aeneas.

nodes.name: King Ascanius / Iulus (Son of Aeneas & Creusa; Founder of Alba Longa, Dionysius I.65–70)
nodes.role: Founder of Alba Longa & Claimed Ancestor of Gens Julia
nodes.notes: Son of Aeneas & Trojan Creusa; built Alba Longa.

nodes.name: 1. King Silvius Posthumus (Son of Aeneas & Lavinia, 29 yrs)
nodes.notes: Half-brother of Ascanius; ancestor of all Alban Silvii.

nodes.name: 2. King Aeneas Silvius (31 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Silvius.

nodes.name: 3. King Latinus Silvius (51 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Aeneas Silvius.

nodes.name: 4. King Alba Silvius (39 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Latinus Silvius.

nodes.name: 5. King Atys / Capetus I Silvius (26 yrs, Livy I.3)
nodes.notes: Son of Alba.

nodes.name: 6. King Capys Silvius (28 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Atys.

nodes.name: 7. King Capetus / Calpetus Silvius (13 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Capys.

nodes.name: 8. King Tiberinus Silvius (Eponym of River Tiber, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Drowned in the Albula, thereafter named the Tiber River.

nodes.name: 9. King Agrippa Silvius (41 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Tiberinus.

nodes.name: 10. King Romulus / Alladius Silvius (19 yrs, Dionysius I.71)
nodes.notes: Son of Agrippa.

nodes.name: 11. King Aventinus Silvius (37 yrs; Eponym of Aventine Hill)
nodes.notes: Buried on the Aventine Hill.

nodes.name: 12. King Procas Silvius (23 yrs; Father of Numitor & Amulius)
nodes.notes: Father of rightful heir Numitor and usurper Amulius.

nodes.name: 13. King Numitor Silvius of Alba Longa (Grandfather of Romulus & Remus)
nodes.notes: Restored to Alba Longa's throne by grandsons Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: Rhea Silvia / Ilia (Daughter of Numitor; Mother of Romulus & Remus)
nodes.notes: Mother of Rome's twin founders Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: King Amulius of Alba Longa (42-Year Usurper, Dionysius I.71, 76)
nodes.notes: Overthrew Numitor before being slain by Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: Remus (Twin Brother of Romulus, 753 BCE)
nodes.notes: Twin brother of Romulus born to Rhea Silvia.

nodes.name: 2. King Numa Pompilius (Sabine Lawgiver King, 715–673 BCE)
nodes.notes: Instituted Roman religious calendar, temples & priestly colleges.

nodes.name: 3. King Tullus Hostilius (673–642 BCE; Absorbed Alba Longa)
nodes.notes: Destroyed Alba Longa and incorporated its noble Alban clans into Rome.

nodes.name: 4. King Ancus Marcius (642–617 BCE; Grandson of Numa)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Numa Pompilius; built Sublician Bridge & Ostia port.

nodes.name: 5. King Lucius Tarquinius Priscus (+ Tanaquil, 616–579 BCE)
nodes.notes: Initiated Circus Maximus & Cloaca Maxima.

nodes.name: 6. King Servius Tullius (578–535 BCE; Servian Constitution & Walls)
nodes.notes: Reformed Roman centuriate classes; son-in-law of Tarquinius Priscus.

nodes.name: 7. King Lucius Tarquinius Superbus (535–509 BCE; Expelled at Republic's Founding)
nodes.notes: Expelled in 509 BCE by Lucius Junius Brutus, inaugurating the Roman Republic.

nodes.name: Gaius Julius Caesar (100–44 BCE; Dictator Perpetuo)
nodes.role: Dictator of Rome & Great-Uncle / Adoptive Father of Augustus
nodes.notes: Descendant of Gens Julia; crossed Rubicon 49 BCE, wed Cornelia/Calpurnia, fathered Julia & Ptolemy XV Caesarion, adopted Octavian.

nodes.name: Julia Minor (Sister of Julius Caesar; Grandmother of Augustus)
nodes.notes: Sister of Julius Caesar; wed Marcus Atius Balbus and bore Atia.

nodes.name: Atia Balba (Niece of Julius Caesar; Mother of Augustus & Octavia Minor)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Julia Minor & Balbus; wed Gaius Octavius and bore Octavia Minor & Augustus.

nodes.name: Octavia Minor (Sister of Augustus; Wife of Mark Antony; Progenitress of Caligula, Claudius & Nero!)
nodes.role: Key Matriarch Linking Julii, Antonii & Julio-Claudians
nodes.notes: Elder sister of Augustus; bore Antonia Minor by Mark Antony — uniting Julian & Antonian lines in Caligula, Claudius, and Nero!

nodes.name: Emperor Augustus / Gaius Octavius (27 BCE–14 CE; Luke 2:1)
nodes.notes: Adopted heir of Julius Caesar; ruled 27 BCE–14 CE during the birth of Jesus.

nodes.name: Empress Livia Drusilla / Julia Augusta (Wife of Augustus; Mother of Tiberius & Drusus)
nodes.role: First Empress of Rome & Mother of Tiberius
nodes.notes: Mother of Emperor Tiberius and General Drusus the Elder by Tiberius Claudius Nero; wed Augustus for 51 years.

nodes.name: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa (c. 63–12 BCE; Builder of Pantheon & Co-Ruler)
nodes.role: Son-in-Law of Augustus & Maternal Grandfather of Caligula
nodes.notes: Wed Augustus's daughter Julia the Elder, fathering Gaius, Lucius, Agrippina the Elder & Agrippa Postumus.

nodes.name: Julia the Elder (Sole Biological Child of Emperor Augustus)
nodes.notes: Mother of Agrippina the Elder by Marcus Agrippa.

nodes.name: General Nero Claudius Drusus (Son of Livia; Brother of Tiberius; Husband of Antonia)
nodes.role: Stepson of Augustus & Father of Germanicus & Claudius
nodes.notes: Brother of Emperor Tiberius; wed Antonia Minor and fathered Germanicus and Emperor Claudius.

nodes.name: Antonia Minor (Daughter of Mark Antony & Octavia; Mother of Germanicus & Claudius)
nodes.era: 36 BCE – 37 CE (Suetonius Claudius 11; Josephus Ant. XVIII.6)
nodes.role: Matriarch of Three Generations of Roman Emperors
nodes.notes: Befriended Berenice I & young Herod Agrippa I in Rome; bore Germanicus, Livilla & Emperor Claudius.

nodes.name: General Germanicus Julius Caesar (15 BCE–19 CE; Father of Caligula)
nodes.era: 15 BCE – 19 CE (Tacitus Annals I–II; Suetonius Caligula 1–7)
nodes.notes: Son of Drusus the Elder & Antonia Minor; wed Agrippina the Elder, bearing Caligula & Agrippina the Younger.

nodes.name: Agrippina the Elder (Daughter of Julia & Agrippa; Mother of Caligula & Agrippina II)
nodes.notes: Granddaughter of Augustus; mother of Emperor Caligula and Agrippina the Younger.

nodes.name: Empress Agrippina the Younger (Sister of Caligula; Wife of Claudius; Mother of Nero)
nodes.role: Daughter of Germanicus & Mother of Emperor Nero
nodes.notes: Great-granddaughter of Augustus; mother of Emperor Nero.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantius I Chlorus (Tetrarch, 293–306 CE; Father of Constantine I)
nodes.role: Western Augustus & Father of Constantine the Great
nodes.notes: Father of Constantine the Great by St. Helena.

nodes.name: Empress St. Helena Augusta (Mother of Constantine the Great, c. 246–330 CE)
nodes.era: c. 246–330 CE (Eusebius VC III; Chronicon Paschale)
nodes.notes: Mother of first Christian Emperor Constantine I.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantine II (Son of Constantine I, 337–340 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Gaul, Spain & Britain after 337 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Constantius II (Son of Constantine I, 337–361 CE)
nodes.role: Middle Son of Constantine & Eastern Emperor
nodes.notes: Ruled the Eastern Roman Empire 337–361 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Constans I (Son of Constantine I, 337–350 CE)
nodes.notes: Ruled Italy, Africa & Illyricum.

nodes.name: Emperor Arcadius (Elder Son of Theodosius I, 395–408 CE; Chronicon Paschale p. 80)
nodes.role: First Emperor of Permanently Divided Eastern Roman Empire
nodes.notes: Proclaimed Augustus by father Theodosius I at the Hebdomon in Constantinople (383 CE); father of Theodosius II.

nodes.name: Emperor Honorius (Younger Son of Theodosius I, 395–423 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Theodosius I & Aelia Flaccilla.

nodes.name: Empress Galla Placidia (Daughter of Theodosius I; Queen of Visigoths & Augusta, c. 390–450 CE)
nodes.role: Daughter of Theodosius I & Mother of Valentinian III
nodes.notes: Daughter of Theodosius I & Galla; wed Visigothic King Athaulf and later Emperor Constantius III.

nodes.name: Emperor Valentinian III (Son of Galla Placidia, 425–455 CE)
nodes.notes: Western Emperor during Attila's campaigns.
